<reason>B won a close, high-quality clash by keeping the vote on the motion as a rights claim: the file is the adoptee’s civil origin, the child never consented to secrecy, and ordinary anti-contact tools are the residual privacy regime. A was vivid on digital identifiability, irreversible outing, and reliance, but never neutralized the consent asymmetry or showed why intermediaries are more than the original veto. B also converted A’s pipeline and “ask, don’t seize” path into illegitimate recruitment rather than a reason to deny an adult the facts of birth.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s first rebuttal that mutual-consent registries are “sealed records with a waiting room,” paired with refusing to withhold origins to keep a placement pipeline, most damaged A’s live middle path; A’s paper-equals-person / stalk-first replies were the strongest counter but did not retake the comparison.</best_rebuttal>
